other_conflicting_accesses: epilogue shared-memory stores/loads on the aliased union: kernel_forward.h L1115-1120 `Epilogue epilogue(shared_storage.epilogue_shared_storage(), ...); epilogue(rescale, dest_iter, accum_o, source_iter);` (SharedStorageEpilogueInLoop, after_mm0.epilogue, kernel_forward.h L556-576) and kernel_forward.h L1164-1169 (kKeepOutputInRF; SharedStorageEpilogueAtEnd union of mm0/after_mm0/epilogue, L534-554). The st.shared/ld.shared themselves are in the CUTLASS submodule (third_party/cutlass epilogue), not in the files of this record; their lines were not examined.

next key block's Q*K^T GEMM: kernel_forward.h L796 `mma(gemm_k_iterations, accum, iterator_A, iterator_B, accum);` whose cp.async writes go into shared_storage.mm0 (mm0 overlaps after_mm0 in the union), and prologueV(0) at kernel_forward.h L800 (same _prologue write at mma_from_smem.h L991). For the gmem instance (kSingleValueIteration false) MM0::Mma is DefaultThreadblockMma = cutlass::gemm::threadblock::MmaMultistage from the third_party/cutlass submodule (kernel_forward.h L408-411, find_default_mma.h L69 / L150), not CustomMmaMultistage, so its cp.async lines are in the submodule, not in custom_mma_multistage.h (whose L319/L322/L355/L358/L403/L431 are used only by kSingleValueIteration instances via MakeCustomMma).
thread_pair_example: not uniquely nameable from the source (CUTLASS thread maps), as stated by verify.thread_pair. Shape of the pair: in iteration blockN of the attn@V loop (kernel_forward.h L1014), thread t of warp A issues cp.async at mma_from_smem.h L952 in the last mainloop iterations (via L1188/L1198) and leaves mma_pv::operator() with up to kNumStagesConcurrentLoad-1 groups pending; every thread passes __syncthreads() at kernel_forward.h L1044 (which does not wait for cp.async); thread u of another warp B then issues the cp.async of prologueV(blockN+1) (L1047 -> mma_from_smem.h L991) or, in the in-loop epilogue (L1115-1120) / the next key block (L796), writes/reads the aliased shared union, while warp A's pending cp.async have not been waited for. The first cp_async_wait after that point is at mma_from_smem.h L1061 (next mma_pv) or inside the next mm0 mainloop.
class_reason: Both listed sites are cp.async writes, which are weak (non-volatile, non-atomic) writes whose completion is ordered only by cp.async.wait_group; __syncthreads() does not order them. No access in the pair is volatile or atomic (verify.strong_accesses: none), so by D20 the pair is DR (not SC). A detector must model cp.async groups and wait_group: if it treats cp.async as a synchronous write at issue it sees no race.
buggy_expected: DR (WAW, shared, cross-warp) between the cp.async write at mma_from_smem.h L952 (stale, no cp_async_wait<0> before MmaMultistageFromSharedMemory::operator() returns) and the cp.async write at mma_from_smem.h L991 (prologueV(blockN+1)), and/or RAW/WAW against the epilogue / next-block shared accesses on the aliased union (see other_conflicting_accesses). The fix commit's racecheck on H100 reports 8 errors (m=129, k=512, fp16), 4 errors (m=64, k=512), 0 hazards when nBlockN == 1 (k=128) and 0 errors + 8 warnings for k=256; the hazard type/lines are not stated in the commit message.

fixed.reason: The fix adds a static drain_cp_asyncs() (cp_async_fence(); cp_async_wait<0>(); __syncthreads();, fixed mma_from_smem.h L932-938) and calls it at fixed kernel_forward.h L802 (else-branch of `if (kPreloadV)`, i.e. only when kPreloadV is false), L1064 (before the in-loop epilogue, replacing the commented-out TODO) and L1171 (before the kKeepOutputInRF epilogue). The commit message reports 0 errors but still 8/8/4 warnings after the fix for fp16 (m=129 k=256, m=129 k=512, m=64 k=512) and 0 hazards for float32 k=512; the sites of those warnings are not given. Program order in the fixed file is mma_pv (fixed L1045) -> __syncthreads (fixed L1046) -> prologueV(blockN+1) (fixed L1049) -> drain (fixed L1064): the drain is placed AFTER prologueV(blockN+1), so the pair (stale write, prologueV write) is not separated by a cp_async_wait<0>/barrier by the fix itself (the next wait is the cp_async_wait<kNumStagesConcurrentLoad - 1> at fixed mma_from_smem.h L1073); the pairs against the epilogue and against the next key block's mm0 are ordered by the drains. Which pair the residual warnings belong to cannot be established from the sources.

kPreloadV is true for 16-bit types on sm80+ (kernel_forward.h L115-116), so for the fp16 sm80 instance the fix's L802 drain is NOT executed (it is in the `else` of `if (kPreloadV)`); only L1064 and L1171 apply.

cp_async_zfill/cp_async lowering (LDGSTS.E.BYPASS... and its line attribution in -lineinfo SASS, which may point into third_party/cutlass instead of the repo files above) not checked; kCacheOpB1 (ca/cg) not determined.

Race manifests as wrong output / NaN only on consumer Ampere/Ada parts (xformers #1392); not observable on H100 in 2000 runs (dispute_points). Detection must be by happens-before modelling of cp.async groups.

Review finding (2026-10-20): both mm1 cp.async writes (L991 of the earlier and of the later prologueV, or L952 vs L991 in the float32 instance) use the same thread map (SmemIteratorB1 built from thread_idx only, mma_from_smem.h L921; this->smem_iterator_B1_ in the operator), so for a given shared address the stale write and the new write come from the SAME thread. A cross-thread report therefore needs an access with a different thread map on the aliased union (warp-level LDSM reads of mm1, the MM0 GEMM or B2bGemm `si` stores that alias mm1 through mm0, or the epilogue); which one racecheck saw is not stated in the commit and is not derivable from the source. Under PTX two cp.async of one thread are themselves unordered, but a detector that reports only cross-thread pairs cannot report that. Observation consistent with the commit's table: for fp16 (kPreloadV) the fix's drain after MM0 (fixed L802) is in the else-branch and does not run, and fp16 keeps 4-8 warnings after the fix while float32 (kPreloadV false, drain runs) goes to 0 hazards; the residual may therefore be on the MM0 -> prologueV(0)/si boundary (fixed L796-L800), unverified.
